import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_55/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_55/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_55/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_55/training_3.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source0 and Source1 on ['CountyID', 'CountyName', 'Year', 'ID']
join_01 = pd.merge(
    source0,
    source1,
    on=['CountyID', 'CountyName', 'Year', 'ID'],
    how='inner',
    suffixes=('_x', '_y')
)

# Step 2: Join Source2 and Source3 on ['CountyID', 'CountyName', 'Year', 'ID']
join_23 = pd.merge(
    source2,
    source3,
    on=['CountyID', 'CountyName', 'Year', 'ID'],
    how='inner',
    suffixes=('_x_10', '_y_14')
)

# Step 3: Join the result of join_01 with join_23 on ['CountyID', 'CountyName', 'Year', 'ID']
# But note that join_01 has columns CountyID_x, CountyName_x, Year_x, ID, CountyID_y, CountyName_y, Year_y, etc.
# join_23 has CountyID_x_9, CountyName_x_10, Year_x_12, ID, CountyID_y_13, CountyName_y_14, Year_y_16, etc.

# To join join_01 and join_23, we need to join on the keys that correspond.
# The keys in join_01 are CountyID_x, CountyName_x, Year_x, ID (from source0)
# The keys in join_23 are CountyID_x_9, CountyName_x_10, Year_x_12, ID (from source2)
# So join on join_01.ID == join_23.ID

final_join = pd.merge(
    join_01,
    join_23,
    on='ID',
    how='inner',
    suffixes=('', '_drop')  # to avoid duplicate columns, but we will drop _drop columns if any
)

# Drop any duplicated columns with _drop suffix if exist
drop_cols = [col for col in final_join.columns if col.endswith('_drop')]
final_join.drop(columns=drop_cols, inplace=True)

# Now rename columns to match the target schema exactly:
# Target schema:
# ['CountyID_x': integer, 'CountyName_x': string, 'whites_population': integer, 'Year_x': integer,
#  'ID': integer,
#  'CountyID_y': integer, 'CountyName_y': string, 'other_population': integer, 'Year_y': integer,

# The columns in final_join should be:

# CountyID_y, CountyName_y, other_population, Year_y,
# From join_23:
# CountyID_x_9, CountyName_x_10, mixed_population, Year_x_12,
# CountyID_y_13, CountyName_y_14, aian_population, Year_y_16

# Check if all these columns exist, if not, fill with NaN or appropriate values

    'CountyID_y', 'CountyName_y', 'other_population', 'Year_y',

    'CountyID_y_13', 'CountyName_y_14', 'aian_population', 'Year_y_16'
]

# Some columns might be missing if join_23 columns have different names, so rename join_23 columns accordingly:
# join_23 columns are:
# ['Unnamed: 0', 'CountyID_x_9', 'CountyName_x_10', 'mixed_population', 'Year_x_12', 'ID',

# We merged on ID, so 'Unnamed: 0' is dropped/not present in final_join.
